stem: A maintenance team needs an application where technicians record inspections of equipment. Each inspection belongs to one piece of equipment and is performed by one technician, and supervisors must see each machine's inspection history. How should the Ontology be modeled before any screen is designed?

choices.text: An Inspection object type keyed on the equipment name, so that each machine has exactly one inspection object updated in place
Separate object types per equipment category, each with its own inspection properties, so screens can be tailored to each category
An Inspection object type with its own key, linked many-to-one to Equipment and to Technician, so history is a link traversal
A single Equipment object type with a list property holding inspection dates and a second list holding technician names in the same order

stem: A supervisor can open a purchase request in a Workshop module and see all its properties, but the Approve button is unavailable for them while a colleague with the same role can approve. What should the developer check first?

choices.text: Whether the supervisor's browser is outdated, since unavailable buttons are usually a rendering problem in older browsers
The Action's permissions and submission criteria against this user and object, since viewing an object does not grant permission to act on it
Whether the object type's backing dataset is stale, since stale data always disables Actions for every user who opens the object
Whether the Workshop module needs to be republished, since buttons only appear for users who opened the module after its last publish

stem: A team needs a function that computes a shipment's estimated cost from weight, distance and a tariff table, returns the same result for the same inputs, and will be maintained by engineers who already write TypeScript. Which paradigm fits?

choices.text: AIP Logic, since any function that reads Ontology data should use a language model to interpret the inputs flexibly
A Workshop variable with a formula, since all calculations belong in the application layer rather than in Functions
A scheduled pipeline transform that precomputes every possible combination of weight, distance and tariff in a dataset
A TypeScript v2 function, since the logic is deterministic, the team knows TypeScript, and no LLM capability is needed

stem: A Workshop module loads slowly. The developer finds that a hidden tab contains several object tables and charts whose variables are computed on page load even though most users never open that tab. What change addresses this most directly?

choices.text: Load the hidden tab's widgets and variables only when it is opened, and trim unneeded variable dependencies
Upgrade every user's laptop so that the browser can compute the hidden tab's variables faster on page load
Duplicate the module into two separate modules and ask users to choose which one to open each morning
Remove the hidden tab and its widgets entirely, since any content that most users do not open is unnecessary

stem: A partner-facing web portal built with the OSDK runs on the partner's servers and must call Foundry to read a curated set of objects with no end user signed in to Foundry. How should authentication be set up?

choices.text: Embed a Foundry user's personal token in the portal's front-end code, since the portal needs some credential to call the platform
Grant the application access to every object type in the Ontology so that scope errors never occur in production
Use a service-based (client credentials) application with scopes limited to the needed object types, with the secret held server-side
Ask each partner to sign in with a shared Foundry account whose password is published in the portal's help page

stem: An automation sends a shipping notice to an external carrier API when an Order becomes "Ready". Because execution is at least once, the same order occasionally produces two notices. What design makes the effect safe?

choices.text: Add a five-minute delay before the effect so that duplicate triggers have time to cancel each other out
Ask the carrier to ignore duplicate notices manually when their staff notice two messages for the same order
Disable retries on the automation so that each Ready transition can only ever be processed one time
Make the effect idempotent with a per-order idempotency key and a notified status checked first

stem: An engineer used AI FDE to generate a TypeScript function that updates order statuses. It compiles and passes a quick manual test, but the reviewer notices it loads every order in the Ontology and filters them in memory. What should happen before publishing?

choices.text: Publish it, since compiled code that passes a manual test is ready for production regardless of how it was generated
Rework it to platform idioms (server-side filtering, pagination, bounded edits), add tests, check side effects
Replace the function with a Workshop button that asks users to update each order's status by hand instead
Ask AI FDE to regenerate the function repeatedly until a version appears that the reviewer does not object to

stem: An automation creates follow-up tasks on objects that the user whose change triggered it cannot see. The user is confused, and an auditor asks how this is possible. What explains it, and what should be reviewed?

choices.text: The automation runs under its own execution identity; review that identity's permissions and who can see the tasks
The platform has a bug that leaks hidden objects to automations, and the automation should be disabled until it is fixed
The triggering user must secretly have access to the objects, and their permissions should be removed immediately to be safe
Automations always run as administrators, so nothing can or should be reviewed about what they access
